title: Work IQ: Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for agents
summary: Hold: the licensing field and cost rating carry Work IQ API consumption billing over to a release whose licensing the page correctly says is not yet published. The roadmap facts, admin paths and spending-policy API check out; the API warning in the pre-check was a false positive.

claims.claim: The Microsoft IQ documentation hub describes a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ is a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI

claims.claim: The hub brings together four capabilities.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ brings together four interconnected capabilities:

claims.claim: Work IQ provides context on employees, collaboration and workflows.
claims.quote: Work IQ provides live understanding of how employees work, with context on people, collaboration, and workflows.

claims.claim: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business, so agents understand business entities and their relationships, properties, actions, and rules.

claims.claim: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge on the context of policies, authoritative documents, and reusable knowledge bases.

claims.claim: Web IQ provides fresh intelligence from the web.
claims.quote: Web IQ provides AI systems and agents with fresh, real-world intelligence from across the web.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly mapped this roadmap item to the hub or explained the release-specific behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft IQ" "570870" default licensing rollout preview; "Microsoft IQ" "unified intelligence layer". Read record and Microsoft IQ hub; the former gives only its short description and the latter does not identify this release or roadmap item.

claims.claim: Work IQ lets agents access and reason over organisational and business data, context and tools.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ has permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.claim: Work IQ endpoints include A2A, remote MCP and REST.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each Work IQ request is user-scoped and can access only what that user may see or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.
claims.quote: Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace Microsoft Entra authentication.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace OAuth permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tools support reading and creating, updating or deleting data.
claims.quote: Which operations are allowed, such as read, create, update, delete, or action?

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP tenant policy disallows mutation operations by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: "The Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness guide separately says 'Write operations are on by default'; verify the effective setting for your experience." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features as well.

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy API settings tenant toggle; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "Graph" API toggle. Read policy-governance-mcp and search excerpts for MCP overview and tool reference; none supplies a policy-toggle API operation.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are outside the initial MCP policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Microsoft says more granular MCP controls might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: The documented path qualifies the Policy tab with 'when it is available'.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The enablement guide lists a Copilot Studio usage-based billing plan with an assigned Azure subscription and resource group as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The guide names a Global Administrator for the one-time Work IQ setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: The documented one-time tenant setup creates the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview#how-tools-work.
